title: BiomedCLIP: a multimodal biomedical foundation model pretrained from fifteen million scientific image-text pairs
layout_note: Four lettered panels: A (three histograms) and B (circular dendrogram bar chart of image types) on top; C below runs left to right from a PubMed article through 'Microsoft Azure' / 'Azure Databricks' steps to an example CT image and caption feeding image and text encoders and a CLIP similarity matrix; a large grey down-arrow leads to D, a dashed grey frame with three application vignettes.
grouping: Panels marked by bold letters A-D; panel C's pipeline steps are pale-grey boxes behind a vertical bar; panel D is a dashed-border light-grey frame titled by its three task names.
shapes_depth: Flat: encoders are trapezoids (pink image encoder, purple text encoder) with vertical labels; embeddings are small rounded tiles (pink I1..In, purple T1..Tn); the similarity matrix is a grid with the diagonal cells in magenta; a large flat grey block arrow joins C to D.
proposed_highlight: The model sits in the lower right of panel C with the CLIP matrix's diagonal filled magenta and encoders in saturated pink and purple, colours re-used in panel D's classification vignette so the same model is recognised downstream.
lesson: Re-use the exact encoder shapes and colours from the training diagram in the downstream-task panel, so the reader sees the same model applied without a label.
notes: year = arXiv preprint year (v3 2025 printed on the first page; first version 2023); remembered venue NEJM AI 2024/2025 (not verified in this session). Two of four panels (A, B) are dataset statistics, not method.

arrangement.units: A and B (data statistics) side by side on top; C (data pipeline + model) a full-width row; D (applications) a dashed grey frame at the bottom; panels marked by letters, not frames
arrangement.inputs_as: a stack of PubMed article pages with a logo, then a real CT image and its quoted caption in a lilac box
arrangement.losses_at: a 'CLIP contrastive loss' label under the similarity matrix at the right end of panel C
arrangement.shared: the two encoders are redrawn in panel D (classification) in the same pink/purple trapezoids

taxonomy.task: biomedical image-text pretraining for retrieval, classification and VQA

core.what: image and text encoders (pink and purple trapezoids) emit I1..In tiles along the top and T1..Tn tiles down the left of one similarity matrix whose diagonal cells are magenta, labelled 'CLIP contrastive loss'

relations.form: panel C runs left to right: PubMed article stack -> two grey Azure step boxes -> a fanned grey wedge opening onto the CT image and its caption card -> encoders -> matrix
image embeddings index the matrix columns from above and text embeddings its rows from the left, the positive pairs marked by magenta diagonal cells
a heavy grey block arrow drops from panel C into panel D, a dashed grey frame holding three side-by-side application vignettes (retrieval, classification, VQA)
panel D sets three downstream uses side by side under titles, each drawn with its own vocabulary (scatter of modality dots, encoders with a bar chart, image with question and answer)

channels.colour: pink = image side (encoder and I tiles), purple/lilac = text side (encoder, T tiles, caption card), magenta = matched pairs on the diagonal; the same pink/purple encoders are reused in panel D; panels A-B use colour for unrelated chart categories
channels.shape: trapezoids = encoders, small rounded tiles = embeddings, plain grey rectangles = data-pipeline steps
channels.line: solid thin lines fan embeddings into the matrix; one grey block arrow links training to applications
channels.frame: panel D alone gets a dashed grey frame; other panels are marked only by letters

quality.strengths: Panel C draws the compared representations as I and T tiles bordering the similarity matrix with positives coloured, and the real CT slice with its quoted caption shows what a pair is; encoder colours carry over into panel D's classifier.
quality.weaknesses: Dataset statistics (histograms in A, radial chart in B) take the top half, so the method row is compressed into the middle; the data-pipeline boxes are vendor logos rather than operations; the matrix's row labels are inconsistent (rows 3 and n reuse T1/T2), and panel D's three vignettes use unrelated drawing vocabularies.

insights.structure: Data statistics (A, B) take the top half, the data-to-model pipeline (C) a full-width middle row, and downstream tasks (D) a dashed grey frame at the bottom, linked to C by one big grey block arrow.
insights.data: Inputs appear as a stack of PubMed article pages, a real CT slice with its caption in a lilac box, and embeddings as pink I and purple T tiles that index a grid whose diagonal cells are magenta.
insights.emphasis: The model is the only saturated-colour region in panel C (pink and purple trapezoids, magenta diagonal), standing out against the grey Azure step boxes.
insights.flow: Panel C runs left to right from article to encoders to the similarity matrix, then a heavy grey arrow turns the flow downward into panel D's three side-by-side task vignettes.
insights.avoid: Half of the canvas is dataset histograms and a radial chart, so the method diagram is squeezed into a third of the height; and the product logos (PubMed, Azure) add brand noise that a method figure does not need.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
